_comment: OSPP Canonical Form vectors for spec/06-security.md §4.8.1. Each vector gives a JSON input and the EXACT canonical string it must produce. The canonical values are the ORACLE: they were recomputed from the rule text in a third language, with a hand-written escaper cross-checked against an independent JSON encoder, and NOT taken from either SDK's output — a vector generated from an implementation can only prove that implementation agrees with itself. Six of these separate defects that both reference SDKs shipped: key-order-is-utf8-bytes-not-utf16, integer-like-keys-are-not-numerically-ordered, line-and-paragraph-separators-are-literal, separators-are-literal-in-keys-too, del-is-not-escaped, start-service-params-vendor-keys. Re-check: node tools/verify-canonical-form.mjs (also Category 20 of tools/verify-protocol.sh).

vectors.name: worked-example
vectors.why: §4.8.2 verbatim: the one canonical form the spec itself prints.

vectors.name: empty-object-payload
vectors.why: Heartbeat REQUEST. The divergence this fixture exists for: PHP emitted "payload":[] and sdk-ts "payload":{}, so the MACs differed on the most frequent message on the wire.

vectors.name: empty-array-stays-an-array
vectors.why: The other half of the same rule: an empty ARRAY is [] and MUST NOT become {}.

vectors.name: nested-empty-object
vectors.why: The distinction holds at every depth, not just the top level.

vectors.name: key-sort-is-recursive
vectors.why: §4.8.1 step 1: sort at EVERY nesting level.

vectors.name: array-order-is-preserved
vectors.why: §4.8.1 step 1: array element order is preserved; arrays are not reordered. programNumbers is compared as a set by the SERVER, but canonicalization does not reorder it.

vectors.name: bays-topology
vectors.why: A real bays[] declaration: array of objects, each sorted, order kept.

vectors.name: scalars
vectors.why: §4.8.1 step 3: booleans and null emit as true/false/null; integers without leading zeros or a trailing point.

vectors.name: slashes-are-not-escaped
vectors.why: §4.8.1 step 3: characters that do not require escaping MUST be emitted literally.

vectors.name: unicode-is-literal
vectors.why: Same rule: no \uXXXX for characters that do not require escaping.

vectors.name: control-chars-are-escaped
vectors.why: §4.8.1 step 3: control characters, quote and backslash DO require escaping.

vectors.name: key-order-is-utf8-bytes-not-utf16
vectors.why: §4.8.1 step 1 orders keys by the UTF-8 BYTES of the key string. JavaScript's Array.prototype.sort() compares UTF-16 code units, and the two disagree across the BMP boundary: U+1D400 is the surrogate pair D835 DC00, so UTF-16 sorts it BELOW U+FFFD, while its UTF-8 encoding F0 9D 90 80 sorts it ABOVE EF BF BD. sdk-ts emitted these two reversed.

vectors.name: integer-like-keys-are-not-numerically-ordered
vectors.why: The same rule, and the half likelier to fire, because it needs no exotic character. JavaScript objects hold integer-like keys in ascending NUMERIC order ahead of every string key, whatever order they were inserted in, so rebuilding a sorted object throws the sort away for exactly those keys — no comparator can fix it. Byte order is "1" < "10" < "2", because '1' is 0x31 and '2' is 0x32. sdk-ts emitted 1,2,10; ospp-sdk-php emitted 1,10,2. This is ordinary JSON, and it is reachable wherever the protocol does not constrain the keys.

vectors.name: line-and-paragraph-separators-are-literal
vectors.why: §4.8.1 step 3 admits exactly three reasons to escape — control characters, quote, backslash. U+2028 and U+2029 are Unicode categories Zl and Zp, not control characters, and JSON itself mandates escaping only below U+0020, so both MUST be emitted literally. PHP escapes them even under JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE and needs JSON_UNESCAPED_LINE_TERMINATORS as well, because the flag was written to protect a pre-ES2019 JavaScript consumer that could not parse them inside a string literal. That is one host language's hazard, not the protocol's — JSON.stringify has always emitted them literally, so ospp-sdk-php was the side that diverged.

vectors.name: separators-are-literal-in-keys-too
vectors.why: Keys carry the same minimal-escaping rule as values, and they sort on the same UTF-8 bytes: U+2028 encodes as E2 80 A8, so it FOLLOWS both ASCII 'a' (0x61) and 'b' (0x62) rather than preceding them.

vectors.name: del-is-not-escaped
vectors.why: A regression guard rather than a repair — both SDKs already agree here. U+007F DEL is Unicode category Cc, but JSON requires escaping only below U+0020 and §4.8.1 asks for the MINIMAL required escaping, so DEL is emitted literally. Canonicalizers that escape it exist, and would not interoperate with either SDK.

vectors.name: start-service-params-vendor-keys
vectors.why: Both defects on one ordinary message, in message shape rather than in the abstract. StartService.params is a free-form map (schemas/mqtt/start-service-request.schema.json declares no properties and does not forbid additional ones), so vendor keys are unconstrained and may be integer-like or non-ASCII. The other open-object sites on the signed path are DataTransfer.data in both directions and SecurityEvent.details.
